first_executed_number_was_wrong.corpus: Every count in this object describes the 2026-08-01 corpus, on which the bug was found and fixed. They are NOT current: read the measured fields of this file for today's numbers, which are lower.
first_executed_number_was_wrong.what: the first cut of the marker test used `[^`]*field[^`]*`, which matches the GAP BETWEEN two adjacent code spans, so a bare English mention sitting between two unrelated spans scored as marked

_provenance.known_false_positives_not_repaired: `markers_for` treats a field name inside ANY backticked span as a citation, so a backticked PATH or flag containing the name as a hyphen-delimited token (`advisory-interpretation-contract.md`, `--paths`) scores as marked. Underscores are safe. Bias runs the same way as the repaired bug -- it inflates marked. Verified inert on today's corpus (those artifacts cite no inventory declaring that field), so the numbers above stand, but one new artifact quoting `--paths` while citing inventory_nose_clones.py would flip a refusal silently. Also unmodelled: lines with an odd number of backticks (a wrapped span's continuation line inverts code/prose -- zero live instances found) and fenced code blocks (pasted `status: ok` output scores a colon marker; fences exist only under --recursive). Marker attribution is per LINE, not per occurrence, matching the sibling probe's line-granular presence-only count -- read it as `field_mention_residuals.count` in charness-artifacts/probe/2026-08-01-inventory-consumption-floor.json, which tests/test_inventory_marker_rule_measurement.py pins equal to this file's `field_mentions_presence_only`. (This sentence transcribed `190` for two refresh cycles after both probes moved past it.) Raised by the round-2 bounded review and recorded rather than repaired: round 2 is the review cap.
